description: exp12: RANGE-config guard for fast path (closure-scoped bound snapshot, sampled refresh every 64 calls + on every fallback, magnitude gates via digit-count bound) — REQUIRED: pre-guard fast path fails new nondefault-RANGE parity suite (verified). Explored object-property (96), closure (95), sentinel-encoded counter (97) variants; all within load-noise. Metric regressed vs 89 best but 89 was invalid under completed parity suite (config blocks prove wrong output under RANGE=5).

asi.hypothesis: fast path must gate against BigNumber global RANGE config or return wrong values under nondefault config
asi.finding: pre-guard code fails CONFIG_PARITY (returns fast-path result where reference returns 0 under RANGE=5); guard cost ~5-7ms under load, unmeasurable across variants due to load-avg-26 noise
asi.next: verify scaling sweep flat, then stop micro-tuning (noise floor exceeded)

description: exp13: verification re-run of exp12 RANGE-guard closure build (no code change) — 100ms vs 97, within load noise (load avg ~26 on shared box). Confirms stable ~95-105 band under contention; scaling sweep flat.

asi.hypothesis: exp12 result stable under noisy load
asi.finding: 95-105ms band across identical builds; machine contention dominates; micro-tuning below ~5ms unmeasurable today

description: exp14: final verification run after load spike subsided — 99ms, stable within the 95-105 contention band. Session final: 662→~97ms median (85.3% faster), all parity+config suites green, 580 unit tests pass.

asi.hypothesis: stable final number under reduced load
asi.finding: still load-inflated (~50 avg during run); true idle-box number likely low 90s; correctness state final
asi.next: session complete — remaining ideas are sub-noise micro-tuning

description: exp15: exact per-call config semantics — sampled RANGE cache REMOVED per parent review (semantically wrong: next call after BigNumber.config change must obey it). liveRangeBound() reads BigNumber.config().RANGE fresh on every fast-path call; magnitude gates use it and defer to BigNumber. Passes strict suite: config parity, warm-then-change (1-63 warm calls then RANGE:5), interleaved config-per-call, DEBUG=true invalid inputs, 5k/10k-digit huge inputs. Negative control: old sampled version fails this suite. 155ms vs 97 sampled — the price of exactness; performance secondary to parity per review.

asi.hypothesis: per-call BigNumber.config().RANGE read restores exact config semantics at acceptable cost
asi.finding: config() ~0.4us/call in Hermes raises primary from ~97 to ~155ms; still 4.3x faster than 662ms baseline; strict warm-then-change/interleaved/DEBUG parity all green
asi.next: exp16: probe cheaper exact config reads (config string-arg? clone snapshot? measure config() cost standalone in Hermes)

description: exp16: unconditionally-config-safe magnitude class — values with magnitude exponent in [-1,1] (or zero) parse identically under EVERY valid BigNumber config (RANGE validated to |bound|>=1, verified in vendored source; no other knob affects decimal parsing or explicit-arg toFixed), so the per-call liveRangeBound() read is skipped for them (canonical: intLen<=2 shapes; scanner: zero-stripped intDigits<=2 or frac-first-digit-nonzero; exponent: |shiftedExp|<=1 incl. int-leading-zero significands e.g. '0.0005e3'). First cut wrongly reused pre-shift configSafe for exponent inputs ('1e10' passed) — caught by RANGE-5 config suite, fixed with shiftedExp gate reading bound fresh when !safe. New RANGE:1 parity block pins the safe class (20 cases) AND the defer class ('100'/'999'/'0.05'/'1e2'/'1e-2'/'5e-6' all collapse to '0'). 133ms vs 155 exact-per-call-read (14% faster), still exact semantics — no sampling, no caching.

asi.hypothesis: config-independence of small-magnitude values lets the fast path skip the live config read without losing exact semantics
asi.finding: 10/18 corpus inputs are safe-class; primary 155->133ms; first-cut exponent bug caught by config suite proves the harness catches shifted-magnitude errors; |e|<=1 bound is the only fully config-independent threshold since RANGE min |bound| is 1
asi.next: exp17: scaling sweep to confirm flatness under new guard structure; then consider remaining config-read reduction only via sound math, no caching

description: exp17: scaling sweep verification of exp16 guard structure — per-call cost perfectly flat across 2k/8k/32k rounds (0.917/0.917/0.922 us/call), no superlinear growth from the config-safe branches or per-call config reads (GC pressure from config() object allocation amortizes flat). Long-input scaling also linear. Primary 132ms at 8k consistent with 133 official.

asi.hypothesis: new guard structure keeps per-call cost flat (keep condition for exp16)
asi.finding: flat within 0.5% across 4x round scaling; config() allocation does not cause superlinear GC cost
asi.next: exp18: final noise-check reruns to stabilize session-best number, then ideas-file triage; remaining optimization headroom within exact semantics is the 8/18 unsafe-class config reads, only reducible via sound math, none found
